newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian judge seeks report on Sarajevo Pope scare.
newsitem.headline: Italian judge seeks report on Sarajevo Pope scare.

text.p: A magistrate investigating the shooting of Pope John Paul in 1981 has asked Bosnian authorities for a report on the discovery of explosives along his route into Sarajevo, Italian judicial sources said on Tuesday.
The magistrate, Rosario Priore, made the request through the international police agency Interpol and hopes it could yield information that would help in his inquiries, the sources said.

Bosnian federation police removed 23 anti-tank mines connected to a remote control system under a bridge along the Pope's motorcade route into Sarajevo on Saturday just hours before the start of his historic visit to the Bosnian capital.
The explosives were removed before the Pope arrived.

A Turk, Mehmet Ali Agca, is serving a life prison sentence in Italy for shooting the Pope in St Peter's Square in May 1981 in an attack that seriously injured the leader of the world's Roman Catholics.
In 1986, a Rome court acquitted three Bulgarians and three Turks of charges that they conspired with Agca to kill the Pope.

Priore, one of Italy's leading anti-terrorism investigators, is conducting a separate strand of investigations into suspicions that members of the Turkish right-wing Grey Wolves organisation may have helped plan the attack.
Agca, who could become eligible for parole later this year, has given contradictory accounts of the attack in media interviews but said last year that he had acted alone.
